title: Why is yawning contagious? (It isn't about oxygen)
description:
We don't yawn for oxygen: in 1987 psychologist Robert Provine had people breathe pure oxygen and air rich in carbon dioxide, and their yawning didn't change. What does trigger yawns is other yawns: 55% of his subjects yawned at a video of yawns (21% at smiles), and 30% yawned just reading about yawning (11% reading about hiccups).

Sources:
- Yawning (Robert R. Provine), American Scientist 93(6), Nov-Dec 2005 — American Scientist / Sigma Xi: https://www.americanscientist.org/sites/americanscientist.org/files/200510314450_646.pdf
- Yawning: no effect of 3-5% CO2, 100% O2, and exercise (Provine, Tate & Geldmacher, Behav Neural Biol 1987): PubMed record — National Library of Medicine (PubMed): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=pubmed&id=3120687&rettype=abstract&retmode=text

Percentages are from Provine's own lab tests. Robert Provine is named, not depicted. The characters are cartoons, not medical advice. Narration is a synthetic voice (Kokoro-82M). Music generated with ACE-Step 1.5; Some sound effects generated with Stable Audio Open (Stability AI).
